plan: Since this auction structure functions like a second-price auction (the clock rises until only the highest sealed bidder remains, and the price paid equals the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the prize is worth to me, and bidding lower risks losing a profitable auction. Therefore, I will bid $40, my true value, to maximize expected profit.

This is effectively a second-price auction since the ascending clock mechanism means I'll pay the second-highest bid if I win. Bidding my true value ($13) is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher, I risk winning and overpaying relative to my value. If I bid lower, I risk losing profitable auctions. Truthful bidding is optimal here.

Since the sealed bid acts as my exit price in an ascending clock auction (equivalent to a second-price auction), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.
